display.purpose: The one heading on the dashboard — '34 HELD'. Carries itself; no kicker plate above it.

headline.purpose: Page titles such as the calendar month. Set globally on main h1.

title.purpose: The account name inside the identity mark; wraps to two lines rather than truncating.

body.purpose: All operator prose at the 15.5px/1.55 base.

body-dense.purpose: The two-line note excerpt in a forme row, 62ch measure.

label.purpose: Every legend in the product; cut into the dark panel with a shadow above and a light lip below.

slug.purpose: The bordered status chip and the default action button.

hour.purpose: The scheduled hour at display scale in the forme row.

readout.purpose: Elapsed counters, delivery tallies, calendar day numbers, npubs, relay URLs.

shadows.name: lamp-recess-dark
shadows.purpose: An unlit indicator lamp on the dark chassis: a well drilled into the panel.

shadows.name: lamp-recess-light
shadows.purpose: The same unlit lamp on warm stock.

shadows.name: cell-recess-dark
shadows.purpose: An unlit poll-strip cell: a relay that did not take the event.

shadows.name: bulb-bone
shadows.purpose: A lit nominal lamp. Restrained — nominal illuminates barely, and only when it is a lamp.

shadows.name: bulb-alarm
shadows.purpose: A red lamp or a red poll cell.

shadows.name: bulb-wait
shadows.purpose: An amber lamp: something is waiting on a human.

shadows.name: engraving
shadows.purpose: text-shadow that cuts legend into the dark panel.

shadows.name: popover-drop-dark
shadows.purpose: The only true drop shadow in the system: the detached flatpickr overlay, dark theme.

shadows.name: popover-drop-light
shadows.purpose: The same detached overlay on warm stock.

motion.name: colour-only
motion.purpose: The default. State changes shift colour; nothing scales, lifts or bounces.

motion.name: panel-slide
motion.purpose: The mobile navigation panel sliding in from the rail edge.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one action a human must take on a screen; the only amber plate.

components.name: Slug Button

components.name: Status Slug
components.description: Record state as an engraved bordered chip. Nominal is unfilled neutral; only waiting-on-a-human (amber) and short delivery (red) carry colour and a wash.

components.name: Indicator Lamp
components.description: The signature element. Four states, one doctrine: off is the default, because nominal does not illuminate. Always aria-hidden; the text beside it carries the meaning.
components.css: .ds-lamp { display: inline-block; width: 9px; height: 9px; border-radius: 2px; background: #413c35; box-shadow: inset 0 1.5px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.75), 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.05); margin-right: 10px; flex: none; } .ds-lamp--lit { background: #cfc7bb; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.35), 0 0 5px rgba(207,199,187,0.22); } .ds-lamp--wait { background: #f0a017; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,225,170,0.4), 0 0 9px rgba(240,160,23,0.5); } .ds-lamp--alarm { background: #d93b1e; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,180,160,0.45), 0 0 9px rgba(217,59,30,0.5); }

components.name: Poll Strip
components.description: Delivery as a poll of N relay stations: one cell per relay, filled for accepted, recessed for declined, red only when the delivery as a whole grades thin or none. The tally is spelled out beside it.
components.html: 5/6
components.css: .ds-poll { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; } .ds-poll-cells { display: inline-flex; gap: 3px; vertical-align: middle; } .ds-poll-cells > i { display: block; width: 13px; height: 17px; background: #413c35; box-shadow: inset 0 1.5px 3px rgba(0,0,0,0.7), 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.05); } .ds-poll-cells > i.is-ok { background: #cfc7bb; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.4), 0 1px 0 rgba(0,0,0,0.5); } .ds-poll-cells > i.is-short { background: #d93b1e; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,180,160,0.45), 0 0 10px rgba(217,59,30,0.55); } .ds-poll-tally { font-family: "JetBrains Mono", ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace; font-weight: 700; font-size: 13px; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: #a49b8c; }

components.name: Identity Mark
components.description: Wire + chop + name, identical on every surface. The 3px wire ink is derived from the account's pubkey so it can never reshuffle; it sits in the row's own flow, never as a border on a container. No npub — the name is the identifier.
components.html: PPluto Broadcast

components.name: Rail Navigation Item
components.description: An engraved route on the chassis rail with an indicator lamp at its head. No icons: a console labels a control with type and an indicator. The active item takes an inset amber spine and a lit amber lamp.
components.html: DashboardPostsCalendar
components.css: .ds-rail { display: block; width: 240px; background: #211f1c; border-right: 1px solid #171512; padding: 8px 0; } .ds-rail-item { display: flex; align-items: center; font-family: "Barlow Condensed", "Barlow", sans-serif; font-weight: 500; font-size: 12px; letter-spacing: 0.16em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #a49b8c; text-decoration: none; padding: 10px 12px 10px 16px; transition: color 150ms, background-color 150ms; } .ds-rail-item:hover { color: #ede8e0; } .ds-rail-item.is-active { background: rgba(240, 160, 23, 0.08); color: #ede8e0; box-shadow: inset 3px 0 0 #f0a017; } .ds-rail-item:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #f0a017; outline-offset: -2px; }

components.name: Text Field
components.description: A plain rectangle with a hairline stroke. Focus shifts the border to amber and adds an amber ring; the caret is amber everywhere in the product.
components.css: .ds-input { width: 100%; font-family: "Barlow", ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14.5px; color: #383430; background: #faf7f2; border: 1px solid #bbb3a6; border-radius: 0; padding: 8px 12px; caret-color: #f0a017; transition: border-color 150ms, box-shadow 150ms; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #6e665a; } .ds-input:focus { outline: none; border-color: #f0a017; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px rgba(240, 160, 23, 0.4); }

components.name: Alarm Block

narrative.overview:
Emanator is a control console for events its operator already signed. The surface is built like the front of a rack-mounted station panel: a warm graphite chassis with the working field as a lighter panel face set into it, structure carried by hairline rule and engraved legend, and a small population of indicator lamps that are dark until something needs a person. There are no cards, no rounded containers, no drop shadows on structure, no stat tiles, and no icons in the rail — a console labels a control with engraved type and an indicator, not a glyph.

The governing doctrine is chromatic scarcity. Nominal does not illuminate. The product has exactly two chromatic values: amber (#f0a017) means a human must tap something, red (#d93b1e) means something did not land. Everything else — every 'published', every 'scheduled', every 'success' — is bone or steel. This is enforced at token level, not by convention: the green, emerald, teal, indigo, blue, sky, cyan, pink and purple ramps are remapped onto the warm neutral scale, so a text-green-500 left anywhere in the markup resolves to #a79e91 and simply stops shouting. The same trick squares the world: every --radius-* token except --radius-full is 0px. The system works by redefining Tailwind's own tokens rather than overriding its classes — there is no !important layer and no per-view patching.

An earlier rendition of this world used a mint/coral/gold semantic trio on a grey-green ground, and was rejected in the user's own words as reading 'AI generated'. That palette is the category default; reaching for it again reproduces exactly the complaint this world answers. It stays rejected, and so does a light 'painted panel grey' chassis. Both shipped themes are approved: the dark chassis is the primary identity and the light theme is its printed twin — the same engraved legend, lamps and rules rendered as ink on warm stock (#efebe4), not a second world. Per-user system/light/dark preference is a product constraint and must survive any change here.
keyCharacteristics: Nominal states are dark; only an exception carries colour.
Exactly two chromatic values, reserved absolutely: amber = act, red = short.
Zero corner radius everywhere except avatars (--radius-full is kept because faces are round).
Structure is hairline rule and engraved legend — never a card, never a shadow.
Delivery is a poll of N stations, rendered as a strip of lamps and a tally, never as a boolean tick.
Warm neutrals throughout; no cool grey, no pure white, no pure black.
Three self-hosted families (font-src :self): condensed caps for legend, Barlow for prose, mono tabular for every measurement.

rules.name: The Nominal Does Not Illuminate Rule
rules.body: A lamp is dark until something is wrong. Green for 'fine' is forbidden — which is why the green/emerald/indigo/blue/purple ramps are remapped onto the neutral scale at token level rather than left available.

rules.name: The Two Chromatics Rule
rules.body: Amber means a human must tap something; red means something did not land. Nothing else in the product may wear either — not identity inks, not avatars, not filter states, not step markers, not unread counts. Each of those was a real violation found and removed during finish review.

rules.name: The Poll Is Not A Boolean Rule
rules.body: Publishing to N relays is a poll of N stations, so a partial answer is the normal answer. :partial delivery is information, never an alarm; only :thin (1 of >=4) and :none light red. An alarm that fires on the ordinary case is an alarm the operator learns to ignore.

rules.name: The Measurement Is Mono Rule
rules.body: Times, tallies, counters, npubs, event ids and relay results are set in JetBrains Mono with tabular numerals. Prose is never mono; a number that must be compared between rows is never proportional.

rules.name: The No Kicker Rule
rules.body: No eyebrow, no kicker plate, no label strip above a heading. The direction contract's FIRST VIEWPORT specified an engraved 'PRESS RUN · NEXT 24 HOURS' plate above the display heading; it was deliberately not built, and the contract was amended rather than the ban overridden. A heading carries itself and its scope line sits below it.

rules.name: The Flat Chassis Rule
rules.body: Surfaces never lift. If a region needs to read as distinct, change its tone or draw a rule — never add a shadow. Shadows belong to lamps, cells and engraving, plus the one detached popover.

rules.name: The Recess-Before-Colour Rule
rules.body: An off state is a well, not a grey dot. An unlit poll cell already says 'this relay did not take it'; red is spent only when the delivery as a whole is alarming.

dos: Do leave nominal dark. A published, scheduled or completed thing gets bone or neutral ink and no lamp glow.
Do change the world by redefining a token in @theme, not by adding an override class. That is how the neutral ramp, the squared radii and the defanged semantic ramps all work.
Do spend amber on exactly one thing per screen: the action a human must take.
Do render delivery as a poll — a strip and a tally — and grade it from publish_results via RelayDelivery, never from status.
Do put the action that belongs to a state inside the row that shows it.
Do set every measurement (time, tally, npub, relay, event id) in JetBrains Mono with tabular numerals.
Do carry both themes on every new surface, including vendored widgets, and keep the per-user system/light/dark preference working.
Do self-host any new font file under public/fonts/; the CSP is font-src :self.
Do use hairline rule and tone to divide regions.
donts: Don't use green, emerald, teal, blue, indigo, sky, cyan, pink or purple. They are remapped to neutral at token level; reaching for one produces a dead grey, which is the intended answer.
Don't put amber or red on anything that is not an action or an alarm — not identity inks, not avatars, not filter chips, not step markers, not unread counts.
Don't treat a :partial delivery as a failure. 5 of 6 is a successful publish and must read as one.
Don't render an unqualified success tick for a publish. The tally always accompanies the verdict.
Don't introduce a card, a rounded container, or a drop shadow on structure. Radius stays 0 except --radius-full for avatars.
Don't add a kicker, eyebrow or label plate above a heading.
Don't mark a row with a 3px coloured border-left; use a tint, a lamp and a slug.
Don't add icons to the rail, or use a glyph where an engraved legend and a lamp will label the control.
Don't reintroduce the rejected mint #7BE0A0 / coral #E04B3C / gold #E8B84B trio, or any variant of the category's default semantic status set.
Don't theme a control under .dark only.
Don't truncate an npub as an identity label; the name is the identifier.
